description: Server-driven reminder system for stale assigned tickets, with brrr as the first delivery channel. Split reminder detection from the web request lifecycle so the app can nudge the primary assignee about aging work without turning the web app into a full PWA yet.

timing.gatingCondition: Can proceed immediately. Requires a brrr webhook secret before end-to-end delivery testing.

principles: Detect staleness on the server, not in the browser
Run reminder evaluation from a separate scheduled process, not tied to web traffic
Start with one-user value: Evan as primary assignee
Keep delivery channels pluggable so web push or family-wide onboarding can follow later
Prefer gentle, actionable nudges over noisy notification spam

techStack.runtime: Express for app, standalone Node script for reminder runner
techStack.scheduler: systemd timer or cron on the Ubuntu host

userStories.title: Store notification channels for family members
acceptanceCriteria: A member can have zero or more notification channels
Initial supported channel type is brrr
Channel records support enabled/disabled state and optional label
Secrets or subscription payloads are stored server-side and never exposed in normal ticket APIs
userStories.testStrategy: Manual API verification and DB inspection

userStories.title: Track reminder state separately from ticket activity
acceptanceCriteria: Reminder state is stored independently from tickets
Each ticket can track last reminder sent, next eligible reminder time, reminder stage, and snooze state
Resolved and closed tickets are automatically excluded from future reminder sends
Repeated runs are idempotent and do not double-send the same reminder window
userStories.testStrategy: Manual DB setup plus repeated runner execution

userStories.title: Reminder detection runner for stale assigned tickets
acceptanceCriteria: A standalone script evaluates stale tickets without requiring HTTP traffic
Only actionable tickets are considered: open, in-progress, waiting
Initial staleness rules vary by priority (urgent, normal, long-term)
Runner can execute safely on a schedule every 30 to 60 minutes

userStories.title: Send brrr notifications with deep links into FamilyHelp
acceptanceCriteria: Reminder notifications are delivered through brrr using a stored webhook secret
Notification includes a useful title, short stale summary, and deep link to the ticket
Reminder urgency maps to sensible brrr interruption behavior
Delivery failures are logged and do not crash the runner
userStories.testStrategy: Manual send to a real device

userStories.title: Basic admin controls for reminder behavior
acceptanceCriteria: Settings page can enable or disable reminders globally
Settings page can store one or more brrr webhook targets
Settings page can configure initial reminder thresholds per priority
Settings page can configure quiet-hour-friendly behavior such as passive vs active delivery

userStories.title: Ticket-level snooze and reminder visibility
acceptanceCriteria: A ticket can be snoozed until a specific time or for a preset duration
Snoozed tickets are skipped by the reminder runner until the snooze expires
Ticket detail clearly shows when the next reminder is expected or if the ticket is snoozed
Primary assignee can quiet a noisy ticket without resolving it
userStories.testStrategy: Manual browser verification plus runner checks

userStories.title: Foundation for future channels and family-wide onboarding
acceptanceCriteria: Notification sending is abstracted behind a small channel interface
Adding web push later does not require rewriting stale detection
Adding channels for additional family members only requires configuration and UI work, not a new reminder engine
userStories.testStrategy: Code review and targeted manual verification

high: Reminder spam if staleness thresholds and dedupe logic are not carefully designed
Webhook secret handling must be treated as sensitive configuration data
medium: systemd timer or cron deployment wiring must match the home server environment
Deep links need to respect nginx /help/ subpath deployment
low: Current schema already exposes strong staleness signals via updated_at, status, priority, and assigned_to
brrr is intentionally simple and matches the single-user-first rollout

possibleTicketAdditions: last_viewed_at or last_action_at only if updated_at proves too coarse
notes: Keep the first migration narrow. Store reminder bookkeeping outside tickets where possible.
Do not over-model delivery history on day one unless debugging proves it necessary.

initialSuppressionRules: No reminders for unassigned tickets in v1
No reminders for resolved or closed tickets
Skip if reminders are globally disabled

deferredScope: Standards-based web push / PWA install flow
Home Screen manifest and service worker work
Escalation to secondary assignees or parents
